static_traits.name: Jiani
static_traits.social_status: Overall family support but not fully understanding her night-shift challenges; fatigue and irritability from night shifts causing relationship tension with family and friends
static_traits.medical_history: No similar problem experience; never received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good cooperativeness, able to reflect and propose feasible strategies; neutral tone, steady speech rate

basic_info.main_problem: I find it very hard to adapt to night-shift work at the hotel, leading to persistent discomfort and dissatisfaction; stress has gradually risen over the past six months, with negative emotions, frustration, and unhappiness every night at work, and sleep hard to adjust.
basic_info.core_demands: The persistent negative emotions and stress brought by night shifts affect overall health and the ability to 'save money for university', therefore I hope through counseling to relieve stress, adjust sleep, improve night-shift adaptation and mindset; at the same time I try recording positive moments, maintaining a more consistent sleep rhythm, and communicating with family for support.

core_beliefs: I cannot adapt to night shifts
I may not be competent enough for this job

special_situations.event: At midnight while working the hotel night shift, energy is lowest and fatigue worsens
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I never adapt to night shifts, it shows I cannot do it and this job is not for me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Listening to music on duty, taking short breaks to relieve discomfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may never adapt to this night shift

special_situations.event: Realizes others have a more 'normal' daytime schedule while she has to work night shifts
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my schedule is not as normal as others', it shows my situation is unfair and I am not as good as others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Complains and compares, reduces focus on the positive side, and argues with family
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Why am I the only one working these hours? This is unfair

special_situations.event: Small mistakes at work or decreased attention
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have oversights, it means my work is not good enough and I might lose my job
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Intensifies self-criticism and executes tasks tensely in order to avoid mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not do well; I will lose my job sooner or later

special_situations.event: Positive experiences occur during shifts (such as positive interactions with guests, quieter nighttime atmosphere)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Occasional positive experiences do not represent overall improvement, nor show I am adapting better
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores or downplays positive segments; focuses only on the negative
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These good moments do not count; overall it is still terrible

core_conflict.wish: Longs to have a stable routine, feel competent at work, and be understood and supported by family
core_conflict.fear: Fearing losing my job from long-term inability to adapt to night shifts, physical and mental exhaustion, and further worsening family relationships
defense_goal: Reducing anxiety and maintaining basic stability through rational explanations and self-control
Reduces conflict to protect important relationships and job position

object_relations.self_representation: A tired and irritable worker who needs understanding and support
object_relations.object_representation: Family who are supportive but do not fully understand her predicament

object_relations.self_representation: A server who can deliver value in positive interactions

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When family cannot yet understand the difficulties of night shifts or question her emotional reactions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing family ignores my hard work and needs, demanding like outsiders that I 'keep hours like others'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using empathetic and concrete language, first acknowledging their feelings, then inviting them to describe the currently hardest part and controllable small changes; in a gentle tone, avoiding judgment.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When fatigued at midnight, making small work mistakes and engaging in Self-denial
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing external pressure and possible negative outcomes as the evaluation 'I am not good enough'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently slowing the pace, inviting them to distinguish facts from evaluations; using concretizing and normalizing techniques, encouraging them to set achievable micro-goals and self-soothing exercises.

manifestations: Lacking autonomy over scheduling and routines, feeling 'unfair' and restricted
Finding it hard to adjust the circadian rhythm, feeling helpless about night-shift arrangements
outcomes: Declining sleep quality and affected overall happiness

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Overly focuses on mistakes and performance decline at work
Frequently worries about 'possibly losing the job'
Concentrates attention more on negative experiences and ignores positive interactions

exception_events.target_problem: When working night shifts until midnight, the client usually develops intense negative thoughts and emotions, decreased attention, getting irritated more easily over small things, affecting work performance
exception_events.unique_outcome: On certain nights (e.g. when not so tired or having positive interactions with guests), she felt more in control, in a better mood, more focused, did not fall into the usual negative spiral, and performed more stably at work
exception_events.reason: Different situation: lower fatigue level; different relationship: positive interactions with guests; environmental features: the quieter nighttime atmosphere perceived as a positive cue, thus easier to notice the value and positive experiences of work

positive_force: Able to self-reflect and willing to try recording positive moments
Willing to adjust sleep rhythm and actively seek support
Able to notice positive value in work (interacting with guests, quiet nights)
negative_force: Mental filtering and dismissing-the-positive cognitive patterns
Overgeneralizing mistakes and negatively predicting the future
Persistent fatigue and irritability caused by circadian rhythm disruption
Tense family relationships from exhaustion and arguments

target_behavior.behavior: Irritability and concentration difficulties during night shifts (with increased negative automatic thoughts)
antecedent: Hotel night-shift work, especially near the midnight hours
Sleep rhythm hard to adjust; persistent fatigue
When comparing routines with others or thinking of possibly losing the job
target_behavior.core_reason: Long-term difficulty adapting to night shifts and circadian rhythm disruption; generating automatic thoughts of 'I cannot do it / might lose my job' and a sense of unfairness from comparison, reinforcing negative emotions and impaired attention
target_behavior.function: Briefly escapes high-load demands and vents tense and tired emotions, trying to gain a sense of control through self-criticism and vigilance
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, more mistakes; arguing with family leading to relationship tension; further damaged sleep quality and overall well-being
